findings.evidence: Rebuilt DE(r) from the route's own LaTeX and damped the single edge with lem:gadget's chain g_i -> (w, g_{i+1}), g_m -> (w, t_0). Exact rows: p = q_0 = 15/16, q_1 = (3/4)(15/16) = 45/64, giving B = [[1699/1024, -225/128],[-225/128, 481/256]] with det = +7219/262144 > 0, LDL^T PSD -- DE(4) damped by beta = 2^{-2} STAYS in R. The route's printed B = [[1249/1024,-195/128],[-195/128,481/256]], det = -7631/262144, reproduces only with q_1 = (1/4)(15/16) = 15/64, i.e. delivery 1/4; and DE_4_DAMPED_GAME.json indeed has 1 -> 18, 18 -> (19, t0), 19 -> (14, t0), delivering 1/4. findings.result_name: ht:prop-tworounds ("M7 is not a one-round mechanism")
findings.defect: The proposition reproduces exactly under the round-18 driver it names, but its stated content -- that the round-one decisions of rem:tangent-cut are "not a law" -- is an artefact of an implementation detail that is NOT part of rem:tangent-cut's definition. rem:tangent-cut says the mechanism "adjoins the tangent cuts at the 8|C| lexicographic optima"; scripts/round18-verify/hz_wedge.py silently adjoins only those with q(x) > 0. On W_10 seven of the 24 lexicographic optima are exactly w* itself; their tangent cuts are valid at w*, and adjoining them makes M7 fire at vertex 2 at ROUND ONE. rem:tangent-cut's clause "a fixed tie-break among optima is part of the definition" licenses a choice AMONG optima, not the suppression of a cut, so under the literal reading of the paper's own definition W_10 is a round-one decision and the proposition's title claim fails.
findings.evidence: Three independent exact drivers. (a) Replicating hz_wedge.py's tie-break (mylp + point_after + skip q=0): round 0 silent, +17 cuts; round 1 silent, +17 cuts; round 2 fires ('(ii)', action 0) -- the route's claim to the digit. (b) The same driver with skip_q0=False: round 0 silent, +24 cuts; round 1 fires at vertex 2 with ('(i)',0) and ('pair',0), naming successor 6, which w*(6) = 17/30 = w*(2) certifies; every added cut passes the exact validity test sum grad*(w*-x) <= -q(x). (c) A wholly independent implementation (my own simplex, de-duplicated cuts) also fires at round 1. The seven extra cut points were printed and each equals w* = (1/2,8/15,17/30,1/2,23/30,1/2,17/30,19/30) exactly -- so the mechanism's own LPs return the value vector as a basic solution at 7 of 24 cut points, which makes "silence" fragile in a second sense the proposition does not mention. Everything else in the proposition reproduced: stopping, all 8 vertices reachable from 2, w* as printed, vertex 2 the sole value-distinguishing one, B over C=(0,2,3) = [[2,0,-1],[0,15/32,-5/16],[-1,-5/16,37/32]] with det 430/1024 > 0 and lambda_min in (0.213640, 0.213640+2^-56), kappa = 4 by brute force over the 8 selections, round-0 silence under all three Z-seeded readings with the paper's Sep. Scripts: .../r19-audit-handicap-tangent-correctness/m7b.py and m7.py

findings.defect: The lemma asserts, and does not prove, that h_n(v) is the largest expected number of visits over all history-dependent behaviours of both players; the proof establishes only h_n <= kappa*1 from the recursion. ht:lem-sigma then USES the interpretation. GAP, exactly: "for every time-dependent selection sequence (beta_n,...,beta_1) the expected number of C-visits within n steps is at most h_n" -- provable in two lines by induction (1 + Q_{beta_n} h_{n-1} <= 1 + S h_{n-1} = h_n), but not given, and the stronger history-dependent claim in the lemma statement is never needed.
findings.evidence: ht:lem-nonstat's statement names history-dependent behaviours; its proof uses only monotonicity of S and the greedy selection at h_n. ht:lem-sigma's proof line: "The left-hand sides are the probabilities of i further visits under the single non-stationary behaviour (beta_n,...,beta_1), so their sum over i = 0..n-1 is at most h_n". The rest of both proofs I reconstructed and they are correct; n*sigma_n <= kappa held for n = 1..7 on 250 fresh random stopping games in R (my own generator, seed 424242), no violation.

findings.defect: Two matrix-norm facts are used without proof: ||P_a||_2 <= sqrt(||P_a||_1 ||P_a||_inf) and ||M||_inf <= sqrt(k) ||M||_2 for k x k matrices. Under rule 4 each needs its two-line proof; for substochastic P_a the first is immediate from Cauchy-Schwarz (||Pd||_2^2 <= sum_v sum_u P(v,u) d_u^2 <= k ||d||_2^2 by column sums <= k), and the second from ||Mx||_inf <= ||Mx||_2. No error: the constants (1 + 2 sqrt k <= 3 sqrt k for k >= 1) are correct.
findings.evidence: Proof reconstructed line by line: d^T B d = ||Rbar d||^2 - ||Delta d||^2 (rem:handicap-base's identity, checked against frontier.tex l.9536ff); Q_alpha = Pbar + S*Delta with S orthogonal; A - c = (A^2-c^2)/(A+c) >= lambda||d||^2/(A+c); A + c <= (1+2 sqrt k)||d||. Checked on 250 fresh random stopping games in R: no violation of kappa <= 3|C|/lambda, worst ratio kappa/(3k/lambda) = 1/3, matching the route's reported factor-3 margin.

findings.defect: The remark invokes thm:modulator, which requires the class to be solved exactly for stopping PAYOFF GAMES with arbitrary terminal payoffs of bit-size beta, in time p(n,beta). ht:thm-kappa is stated only for stopping SSGs with 0/1 sinks (its proof uses lem:denominator-sharp's D <= 2^a, the 0/1-sink form). GAP, exactly: "the algorithm of ht:thm-kappa extends to every stopping payoff game with rational terminal payoffs of common denominator Delta, in time polynomial in n, K and log Delta". The extension is routine (lem:survival-contract is stated for arbitrary rewards, lem:round-recover carries Delta through Q = 2*Delta*2^a) but it is asserted. The freezing-closure argument itself is correct: freezing a controlled vertex leaves Q' the principal submatrix of Q on C', and freezing an average vertex only shortens first passages, so kappa cannot increase.
findings.evidence: thm:modulator, frontier.tex l.3190: "If P is solved exactly in time p(n,beta) on payoffs of bit-size beta ...". lem:denominator-sharp, frontier.tex l.1259-1265, is the 0/1-sink statement.

verdict:
NOT SOUND: two majors survive, but the route's central mathematics does hold.

WHAT I RECONSTRUCTED AND CONFIRMED CORRECT. (1) ht:lem-sigmin: the proof is right line by line -- the identity d^T B d = ||Rbar d||^2 - ||Delta d||^2 is rem:handicap-base's, every selection is Q_alpha = Pbar + S Delta with S = diag(+-1) orthogonal, A - c = (A^2-c^2)/(A+c) >= lambda||d||^2/(A+c), and A + c <= (1 + 2 sqrt k)||d|| <= 3 sqrt k ||d|| for k >= 1. No violation on 250 fresh random stopping games in R from my own generator (seed 424242); worst ratio kappa/(3k/lambda) = 1/3. (2) ht:lem-sigma: the partial-product argument is correct, and the sub-multiplicativity sigma_{t*n_0} <= 2^{-t} that ht:thm-kappa needs follows from positive homogeneity and monotonicity of S (the route does not spell this out; it is two lines). (3) ht:thm-kappa: correct, including the precision arithmetic -- J = ceil(2K)(2a+3) gives error 2^{-(2a+3)} < 1/(2D^2) with D <= 2^a strictly, so Legendre applies with no boundary case -- and bit sizes do stay polynomial in N and K. I ran the algorithm end to end on 120 fresh random stopping games (exact and certified on all 120) and on HZ(4) (N = 98, a = 80, |C| = 16, all first-passage row masses exactly 1/2, kappa = 2, J = 815 reduced iterations, T_C(yhat) = yhat, values matching the archived w* on C). (4) ht:cor-rlambda: the combination is valid, recognisability by one exact PSD test is right, and the freezing-closure of {kappa <= K} is correct. The separation from thm:escape-class rests on prop:hz and is legitimate; HZ(n) is outside all eight named classes by prop:hz and inside R_{1/4}, so the corollary's content stands. All eight claimed WD/CC rows reproduce exactly. (5) ht:prop-cutform and ht:cor-cutwidth: the identity and both inequalities are correct; verified at 114 point pairs over 40 fresh random games in R, including re-solving the LP with the single cut adjoined -- max u_{v,ibar} * M(v,i) <= q(x) held every time. (6) ht:prop-damping's principal witness: I rebuilt DR(8,38) from the LaTeX (74 vertices, stopping by the trap test, P_0 = P_1 = (255/256)*antidiag, B = [[130561/65536,-255/128],[-255/128,130561/65536]], lambda_min = 1/65536 = 4^-8, both Max vertices value-distinguishing) and its def:damping image with m = 7 (1082 vertices, stopping): det B_rho = -3.751771119649288e-05 and d = (1,15/16) gives d^T B_rho d = -9.174377903533963e-06, the route's numbers to every printed digit; the algebraic rows p = q_0 = rho^2(1-(rho/2)^r)/(2-rho), q_1 = rho^L q_0 agree with the built game entry for entry. Fresh points DR(9,60) (100 -> 1472) and DR(12,120) (172 -> 2552) reproduce. So "R is not closed under damping" is established.

THE TWO MAJORS. (A) The "a single edge suffices" clause of ht:prop-damping is false as written: with def:damping's beta = 2^{-2} (leak 1/4, delivery 3/4) DE(4) has det B = +7219/262144 and stays in R; the route's printed matrix and its built file correspond to delivery 1/4, i.e. a leak of 3/4, which is not a lem:gadget chain. Repairable -- DE(5) with m = 1 is a genuine witness under the paper's convention and is the smallest in the family -- but the instance, the parameter and the "smallest found" claim as printed do not reproduce. (B) ht:prop-tworounds reproduces exactly under the driver it names, but only because that driver suppresses the tangent cuts at lexicographic optima where q(x) = 0, a suppression rem:tangent-cut does not authorise. On W_10 seven of the 24 lexicographic optima are w* itself; adjoining their (exactly validity-checked) cuts makes M7 decide vertex 2 at round ONE, in three independent implementations. So the proposition establishes two-round silence for one implementation of M7, not for M7 as rem:tangent-cut defines it, and its title claim is not established. This is precisely the round-18 failure mode the rules single out: the mathematics under the headline holds, the headline overreaches.

THE ROUTE'S OWN HEADLINE, by contrast, is a sentence it proved: ht:lem-sigmin plus ht:cor-rlambda give exactly "B >= lambda I implies every positional pair visits C at most 3|C|/lambda times in expectation, and R_lambda with lambda >= 1/poly(N) is a polynomial class". I found no defect in it.

MINORS: two asserted steps that should be GAPs (ht:lem-nonstat's history-dependent interpretation, which ht:lem-sigma uses; the two matrix-norm facts in ht:lem-sigmin), the payoff-game extension ht:rem-freeze needs before thm:modulator applies, two unproved general formulas (kappa(WD) = 2^{2j}, kappa(CC) = 4^L) stated as facts, one overstated comparison with prop:hz's contraction rate, and a vertex miscount in games_built. NOTES: kappa is (v11)'s object, not a new one (the proof is new); the Z-seed is vacuous on W_10.

I found no fatal defect, no greedy policy iteration in a non-stopping game, no dict-literal row collapse, no sink collision among fresh vertices, no trap excluding t_0, no vacuous stall, no unreachable vertex used to separate a family, no non-dyadic witness, no unbuilt family (every claimed game exists and I rebuilt each from the statements independently), no oracle that is target-equivalent, and no fifth imported theorem beyond the two elementary norm inequalities noted. No background jobs were started; nothing was written outside /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/c506180a-e393-4ffa-a18f-efc78c98397e/scratchpad/r19-audit-handicap-tangent-correctness.
